results.result: The manuscript provides background on Parkinson's disease (PD), describing it as a common neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive degeneration of dopamine neurons in the substantia nigra (SN) while ventral tegmental area (VTA) neurons remain largely unaffected. Current therapies are symptomatic and not disease-modifying.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C15 are well-established facts about PD supported by appropriate citations to the literature. These background claims accurately represent the current understanding of PD pathology and treatment limitations.

results.result: Elevated metabolic stress plays a central role in SN DA neuron vulnerability, triggered by increased cytosolic dopamine levels, high energy demand from large axonal arborization, and constant intracellular Ca2+ load from continuous electrical activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C20 are supported by appropriate citations to previous literature establishing the role of metabolic stress in SN DA neuron vulnerability. These are well-accepted mechanisms in the field.

results.result: Dendritic Ca2+ transients depend on voltage-gated Ca2+ channels including Cav1.3 L-type channels, which activate at subthreshold potentials and do not completely inactivate during pacemaking. The LTCC blocker isradipine showed neuroprotection in some animal models but failed in the STEADY-PD III clinical trial, with only ~50% of Ca2+ transients blocked by isradipine in dendrites and somatic transients being resistant.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C27 are well-supported by citations to previous work, including the negative STEADY-PD III trial results. This provides important context for why alternative Ca2+ channel targets like Cav2.3 are being investigated.

results.result: Previous work established that Cav2.3 is the most abundant Cav channel in SN DA neurons, contributes to activity-related somatic Ca2+ oscillations, and Cav2.3 knockout is neuroprotective in the chronic MPTP mouse model of PD.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C28-C30 are supported by citations to previous work (Benkert et al., 2019). These establish the rationale for investigating Cav2.3 channel modulation by β-subunits in the current study.

results.result: SN DA neurons are spontaneously active pacemaking neurons with membrane potentials ranging from ~-70 mV to ~-40 mV during regular pacemaking. Cav2.3 α1-subunits were originally cloned as low-voltage-gated channels (V0.5,inact -78 mV), but SNX-482-sensitive R-type currents in different neuronal cell types show wide variation in steady-state inactivation (V0.5,inact ranging from -90 to -40 mV).
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C37 are supported by appropriate citations establishing the electrophysiological properties of SN DA neurons and the heterogeneity of Cav2.3 channel inactivation properties across different neuronal types. This heterogeneity motivates investigation of β-subunit modulation.

results.result: Alternative splicing of Cav2.3 α1 subunits is unlikely to account for large shifts in steady-state inactivation. β-subunits form part of the Cav2.3 channel complex and tightly control V0.5,inact. Cytosolic β-subunit isoforms induce inactivation at negative potentials (complete at >-50 mV), while membrane-anchored β2a and β2e induce strong positive shifts of V0.5,inact and slow voltage-dependent inactivation.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C43 are supported by citations to previous literature establishing the differential effects of cytosolic versus membrane-anchored β-subunits on Cav2.3 gating. This provides the mechanistic basis for the current study.

results.result: In tsA-201 cells expressing Cav2.3e (the only splice variant detected in SN DA neurons), cytosolic β3 and β4 subunits induce rapid inactivation at negative voltages (V0.5,inact < -70 mV, ≥50% within 50 ms). β2a and β2e shift V0.5,inact by ~30 mV to more positive potentials, slow inactivation, and induce window currents at negative potentials. All β-subunits increased current densities 6-12-fold. The β2a shift depends on N-terminal palmitoylation for voltage-dependence but not for slowing inactivation kinetics.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C61 are supported by experimental data in Figure 1 and Table 1, with appropriate controls and statistical analysis. The identification of Cav2.3e as the predominant splice variant in SN DA neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) strengthens the relevance of using this variant for functional studies.

results.result: RT-qPCR analysis of mouse SN and VTA tissue shows β4 (~60%) and β2 (~27%) are the most abundant β-subunit transcripts, with β1 and β3 comprising ~4-7%. Among β2 splice variants, β2a (~30%) and β2e (~26%) together comprise about half of all β2 transcripts, with cytosolic β2c/d comprising ~42% and β2b only ~3%. These findings agree with published RNA-seq data from mouse and human midbrain DA neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C48, C63-C68 are supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 2A-B with appropriate technical controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and agreement with independent RNA-seq datasets. The quantitative PCR approach with standard curves provides robust quantification.

results.result: β2a and β2e subunit transcripts are expressed in mouse SN tissue and in identified SN DA neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C6 are supported by multiple complementary approaches: RT-qPCR (Figure 2), RNAscope in situ hybridization (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), and single-cell RT-qPCR from laser-microdissected neurons (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A). The convergence of multiple methods strengthens confidence in the expression findings.

results.result: During simulated SN DA neuron pacemaking (2.5 Hz) in tsA-201 cells, Cav2.3 channels with β3 or β4 conducted current during AP repolarization but rapidly inactivated (almost completely after 1-2 min). In contrast, β2a and β2e maintained ~40% of initial current after 5 min of continuous activity, supporting current during both AP repolarization and the interspike interval. Remaining currents were completely blocked by Cd2+ with recovery upon washout.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C69-C77 are supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing differential current stability with different β-subunits during physiologically relevant pacemaking protocols. The Cd2+ block and recovery experiments confirm the currents are mediated by Ca2+ channels. The use of actual SN DA neuron AP waveforms as command voltages strengthens physiological relevance.

results.result: Current run-down experiments using square pulses (0.1 Hz) and pacemaking protocols with pauses show that β3-associated Cav2.3 channels exhibit ~45% run-down after 4.5 min, while β2a largely prevents run-down (~16%). Recovery experiments demonstrate that IAP decrease during pacemaking is almost completely due to reversible accumulation of channels in inactivated states, partially prevented by β2a and β2e.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C83 are supported by experimental data in Figure 4 showing differential run-down and recovery properties. The pause experiments effectively distinguish between irreversible run-down and reversible inactivation, strengthening the mechanistic interpretation.

results.result: During simulated burst activity, integrated Ca2+ current was 4-6-fold higher than during steady-state APs with all β-subunits tested. Recovery from inactivation after 1.5 s at -89 mV was ~30% with both β4 and β2a in square-pulse protocols, but recovery during the hyperpolarizing pause after bursts was much less pronounced (β4) or absent (β2a, β2e).
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C84-C86 are supported by experimental data in Figure 5 and Table 2. The findings show that β2a/β2e enhance Ca2+ entry during bursts but do not facilitate recovery during post-burst pauses, providing important insights into channel behavior during different activity patterns.

results.result: In SN DA neurons in brain slices, R-type current (isolated pharmacologically) activated ~8 mV more positive than total ICa, with V0.5,inact of -47.5 mV. SNX-482-sensitive current showed V0.5,inact of -44.6 mV, ~5 mV more negative than recombinant Cav2.3 with β4/β3 but consistent with β2a/β2e modulation. At holding potential of -60 mV (perforated patch), ~13% of total ICa was inhibited by SNX-482 and ~10% by nifedipine.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C49, C87-C88, C92-C95 are supported by experimental data in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1. The voltage-dependent inactivation properties of native R-type currents are intermediate between those observed with cytosolic and membrane-anchored β-subunits in heterologous expression, consistent with a mixed population. The perforated patch experiments demonstrate channel availability at physiologically relevant voltages.

results.result: In cultured mouse DA midbrain neurons, 100 nM SNX-482 reduced non-LTCC currents by 41% (LTCC currents comprised 24.7% of total). SNX-482-sensitive currents activated at V0.5,act of -9.2 mV and inactivated at V0.5,inact of -58.1 mV, which is 12-18 mV more positive than recombinant Cav2.3 with β4/β3, confirming R-type current activity during the pacemaking cycle.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C50, C96-C100 are supported by experimental data in Figure 7. The voltage-dependent properties of SNX-482-sensitive currents in cultured neurons are consistent with modulation by membrane-anchored β-subunits, though more negative than in brain slices. The substantial contribution of R-type currents to non-L-type Ca2+ entry supports their physiological relevance.

results.result: In current-clamp recordings of cultured midbrain neurons, 100 nM SNX-482 significantly reduced spontaneous firing frequency from 4.1±0.8 Hz to 1.1±0.2 Hz, decreased pacemaking regularity, and caused changes in AP shape, suggesting Cav2.3-mediated currents contribute to the pacemaking cycle.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C104 are supported by experimental data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1, but the interpretation is complicated by SNX-482's known effects on Kv4.3 channels. The authors acknowledge this limitation and note that the observed effects (AP shortening, reduced firing) are inconsistent with Kv4.3 block, which typically broadens APs and increases frequency. However, without genetic knockout or more selective tools, the contribution of Cav2.3 versus off-target effects remains uncertain.

results.result: During simulated SN DA neuron-like continuous tonic pacemaking in tsA-201 cells, Cav2.3 channels remained active only when associated with β2a or β2e, but not with cytosolic β3 and β4 subunits. In contrast, steady-state inactivation of Cav1.3 channels was largely unaffected by β2a, suggesting Cav1.3 availability is much less dependent on β2a subunits.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C46 are supported by experimental data in Figure 3 (Cav2.3) and Figure 1—figure supplement 2 (Cav1.3). The differential dependence on β2a between Cav2.3 and Cav1.3 is an important finding showing channel-specific modulation by β-subunits.

results.result: The large shift of V0.5,inact of Cav2.3 R-type current by membrane-anchored β2a and β2e subunits predicts that Cav2.3 channel availability can be adjusted along a wide range of potentials (about 30 mV; V0.5,inact -40 to -70 mV) by varying the abundance and local availability of these subunits relative to cytosolic β-subunits.
results.evaluation: Claim C105 is a reasonable inference from the experimental data showing ~30 mV shifts in V0.5,inact between cytosolic and membrane-anchored β-subunits (Table 1) and the expression data showing both types are present in SN DA neurons. The ~11-14 mV difference in V0.5,inact between cultured neurons and brain slices supports this interpretation.

results.result: Transcriptomic analysis of laser-captured SN DA neurons from 18 human postmortem brains shows 30% β2, 45% β4, 15% β3, 8% β1, in excellent agreement with mouse data.
results.evaluation: Claim C106 is supported by citation to published transcriptomic data (Aguila et al., 2021) and shows good agreement with the authors' mouse RT-qPCR data, supporting conservation of β-subunit expression patterns across species.

results.result: β4-subunits may extensively target to channels at axonal presynaptic locations or to the nucleus, and differences in β-subunit affinity for α1-subunit interaction domains may support preferential association with β2.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C108 are speculative explanations for why β2a/β2e might preferentially associate with Cav2.3 channels at somatodendritic sites despite β4 being more abundant. While supported by citations to previous work, these remain hypotheses that would require biochemical or imaging studies to confirm.

results.result: β-subunit alternative splicing may prevent a fraction of Cav2.3 channels from inactivation in continuously active SN DA neurons, supporting Ca2+ signals contributing to the (patho)physiological role of Cav2.3 channels in PD. Cav2.3-knockout mice are protected in the MPTP/probenecid PD model, suggesting pharmacological inhibition of Cav2.3 alone or with other Cavs may provide neuroprotective effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C10, C109-C111 represent the main conclusions of the study. The inference that β-subunit splicing prevents Cav2.3 inactivation is well-supported by the experimental data. The neuroprotective potential is supported by previous work (C109) and represents a reasonable therapeutic hypothesis based on the findings, though clinical validation would be required.

results.result: Cav2.3-mediated R-type currents are notoriously drug-resistant with no selective small-molecule blocker reported. A neuroprotective strategy could aim at reducing Cav2.3 contribution by interfering with β2a/β2e association. CaVablator has been used to target β-subunits for degradation and strongly reduces Cav1- and Cav2-mediated currents.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C116 are supported by appropriate citations. C112-C113 are established knowledge about Cav2.3 pharmacology. C114 is a reasonable therapeutic strategy based on the findings. C115-C116 cite previous work on CaVablator as a proof-of-concept for β-subunit-targeted approaches.

results.result: Cav2.3 α1-subunit transcripts are the most abundant in mature SN DA neurons. SNX-482 is a potent blocker of Kv4.3 channels (IC50 ~3 nM), which typically induces AP broadening and increased frequency in DA neurons. However, in Cav2.3 knockout mice, only small changes in AP waveforms were observed without major changes in pacemaking.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C122 are supported by appropriate citations. These provide important context for interpreting SNX-482 effects and the role of Cav2.3 in pacemaking. The acknowledgment of SNX-482's off-target effects and the modest pacemaking phenotype in Cav2.3 knockout mice demonstrate appropriate scientific caution.

results.result: β-associated Cav2.3 channels contribute more to overall Cav2.3-mediated currents than channel complexes devoid of β-subunits and can be subject to differential modulation by β-subunits.
results.evaluation: Claim C62 is a reasonable inference from the 6-12-fold increase in current densities with β-subunits (C61, Figure 1A, Table 1), indicating that β-associated channels dominate the functional channel population.
